entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Publius Valerius Falto was a Roman politician of the 3rd century BC.

As a prominent figure in the late Roman Republic, Falto played a key role in the struggle for power among the Roman aristocracy. He collaborated with Lucius Appuleius Saturninus to pass the First Triumvirate legislation, which aimed to curb the growing influence of the equestrian order and promote the interests of the senatorial class.

Falto's actions had significant consequences for Roman politics, contributing to a period of increased instability and factionalism. His legacy can be seen in the eventual rise of the Roman Empire under Augustus Caesar.

One striking statistic is that Falto was one of the key figures involved in the First Triumvirate, which lasted from 60 to 53 BC and had a profound impact on Roman politics.
